title: Node Async, Errors and Shutdown: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of Node async patterns (callbacks, promises, async/await), error-first callbacks, Express error middleware, unhandled rejections, environment config and graceful shutdown.

chapters.title: Callbacks and the Error-First Convention
points: Definition: a callback is a function passed to an async API and called later by the event loop, never inline in the caller's stack
Mechanism: error-first signature is cb(err, result); err is null or undefined on success, so always check err first and return
Comparison: callbacks vs promises. A callback cannot be returned or awaited, and nesting grows into 'callback hell'; promises chain flat
Example: fs.readFile(path, 'utf8', (err, data) => { if (err) return cb(err); cb(null, data) }); util.promisify wraps this style into a promise
Interview Point: Why must errors never be thrown inside an async callback (the try/catch has already exited)? What does promisify require of the callback? What is the double-callback bug?

chapters.title: Promises and async/await
points: Definition: a promise is pending, then fulfilled or rejected exactly once; .then handles success, .catch handles rejection, .finally always runs
Mechanism: async functions always return a promise; await pauses only that function and a rejection becomes a thrown error caught by try/catch
Comparison: Promise.all rejects fast on the first failure; allSettled waits for all and reports each outcome; race settles with the first one; any resolves with the first success
Example: const [a, b] = await Promise.all([getA(), getB()]) runs in parallel, while two awaits in a row run sequentially

Mistakes: forgetting await (the promise is silently dropped), await inside forEach (it does not wait; use for...of or Promise.all with map), and returning a promise inside try without await (the catch is skipped)
Interview Point: Does await block the event loop? How do you run tasks in parallel? Difference between all and allSettled?

chapters.title: Express Error Middleware
points: Definition: error middleware has four parameters (err, req, res, next); Express recognises it by its arity, so keep all four even if next is unused
Mechanism: call next(err) or throw synchronously to skip to the error handler; register it after all routes and app.use calls
Comparison: Express 4 does not catch rejected promises from async handlers, so wrap them or use a catch-to-next helper; Express 5 forwards rejections automatically
Example: app.use((err, req, res, next) => { res.status(err.status || 500).json({ error: err.message }) }), with a custom AppError class carrying status
Mistakes: sending a response twice (check res.headersSent and call next(err)), leaking stack traces in production, and a missing 404 handler before the error handler
Interview Point: How does Express identify error handlers? Why does async code in Express 4 hang on error? Where must the error handler go?

chapters.title: Unhandled Rejections and Uncaught Exceptions
points: Definition: unhandledRejection fires when a promise rejects with no handler attached; since Node 15 the default is to crash the process with a non-zero exit
Mechanism: process.on('unhandledRejection', (reason) => ...) and process.on('uncaughtException', (err) => ...) are last-resort hooks for logging, not for recovery
Comparison: after an uncaughtException the process state is unknown, so log and exit; it is not safe to keep serving as if nothing happened
Example: process.on('unhandledRejection', (r) => { logger.error(r); process.exit(1) }) and let a supervisor (PM2, Docker, Kubernetes) restart it
Interview Point: What changed in Node 15? Why is it unsafe to continue after uncaughtException? Where should errors be handled instead?

chapters.title: Environment Config and Graceful Shutdown
points: Definition: config comes from process.env (strings only); load .env locally with dotenv or --env-file, never commit it, and set real values in the platform
Mechanism: validate env vars at startup (fail fast on missing ones), convert types (Number(process.env.PORT)), and give safe defaults only for non-secrets
Mechanism: on SIGTERM and SIGINT call server.close() to stop accepting new connections, finish in-flight requests, close DB and queue connections, then process.exit(0)
Example: process.on('SIGTERM', () => { server.close(async () => { await db.end(); process.exit(0) }); setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), 10000).unref() })
Mistakes: ignoring SIGTERM in containers (killed after the grace period), keep-alive connections holding server.close open, and exiting before cleanup finishes
Interview Point: Why SIGTERM and not SIGKILL? Why a forced-exit timeout? Why validate env at boot?

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Async, Errors and Shutdown
points: Callbacks: cb(err, result); check err first and return; promisify converts to a promise
Promises: all fails fast, allSettled reports every outcome, race takes the first to settle, any takes the first success
async/await: always await or return the promise; use for...of or Promise.all with map, never forEach
Express: the four-argument handler goes last; next(err) forwards errors; wrap async handlers in Express 4
Process: unhandledRejection and uncaughtException mean log and exit; validate env at boot; SIGTERM, then server.close, then cleanup, then exit with a timeout
